clue.text: Married nursing assistant had babies

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the word for married holds the assistant inside it

parts.note: WED means married
a help is an assistant, as in a home help

explanation.surface: A newly married couple's helper ends up with a family of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing' looks like caring for the babies, but it means holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelp is to give birth, used chiefly of dogs and other animals.

clue.text: Little lad drained of type of blood in scene from Dracula

parts.note: a whit is a very little amount

indicators.note: drained of means emptied of, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a boy is a lad
O is a blood group

explanation.surface: A vampire victim, a small boy drained of blood in Dracula.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitby is a Yorkshire seaside town where Dracula comes ashore in Stoker's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker set key episodes of his vampire novel in this Yorkshire harbour town.

clue.text: Get in a flap at the table

indicators.note: in a flap means flustered, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone gets flustered at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being seated at the table usually means having a meal, so dining is the sense.

clue.text: Man smashed head of Russian moneylender

parts.note: a pawn is a chess man
broke is a past tense of break, as in smashed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man breaks a Russian moneylender's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker lends cash against goods left as security.

clue.text: Wise duke upset top drawer

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down entry the letters run upward

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: A wise duke turns a chest of drawers over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top drawer' looks like furniture; it is a first-rate artist, one who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a leading French painter and draughtsman, a top artist.

clue.text: Introduction to Frinton, not just somewhere to enjoy yourself

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, here of the town name

parts.note: something not just is unfair

explanation.surface: A grumble that Frinton, a sedate English seaside town, is unfairly treated as a place for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground with rides and stalls is a place people go purely for amusement.

clue.text: Trimmings of hair down there, so short

parts.note: fur is an animal's hair
below means down there

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about trimming body hair down below.
explanation.definitionFit: Furbelows are showy frills and ornamental trimmings on clothing.

clue.text: Chap is unfamiliar, but not very

indicators.note: but not means except for, so a letter is left out

parts.note: novel means new and unfamiliar

explanation.surface: A man is a stranger, though not a complete one.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a man's first name, and crosswords use chap for any male name.

clue.text: Dove very softly into a quiet river

indicators.note: into means put inside the other pieces

parts.note: ease means quiet or rest
pp is the musical marking pianissimo, very softly

explanation.surface: A dove dives very softly into a calm river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dove' looks like the verb dived or a bird; it is a peacemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a dove favours conciliation and peace, so someone who placates.

clue.text: Actual, complete sentence

definitions.note: actual means real-world, genuine, as opposed to imagined

parts.note: real can mean complete or utter, as in a real disaster
life is a prison sentence for the rest of one's days

explanation.surface: A grammar point: a genuine, whole sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete sentence' looks like grammar; it is an utter prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: Real-life as an adjective means genuine and actual rather than fictional.

clue.text: Keen on wife following close behind

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone fond of their wife trails along just behind her.
explanation.definitionFit: Having someone in tow means they are trailing along behind you, like a towed vehicle.

clue.text: Gadarene stampede to check p-pulse

indicators.note: a stampede is a wild disordered rush, so the letters run riot

parts.note: the stutter at the start of the last word supplies a lone letter P

explanation.surface: The Gadarene swine of the Gospels stampede, apparently enough to make one's pulse stutter.
explanation.walkthrough: The stuttered 'p-' before 'pulse' is the extra letter mixed with GADARENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes, and the garden pea is a common example.

clue.text: I'm lost for words after recollecting swelling bosom in steamy novel

indicators.note: after places the hesitation sound at the end, following the other pieces
re-collecting suggests gathering again from the back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a knob is a rounded swelling or lump
bust is another word for bosom
er is what a speaker says when lost for words

explanation.surface: A reader struggles for words over a heaving bosom in a racy novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonkbuster is British slang for a raunchy, bestselling novel full of sexual encounters.

clue.text: Alcohol-related trouble

indicators.note: related in the sense of told or recounted, so the word is spoken

parts.note: ale is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A problem caused by drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Related' means narrated, not connected: ALE spoken gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, as in asking what is troubling someone.

clue.text: Worry about extremely exploitative figure in capitalist system

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: fret means worry

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme, outermost letters of the word

parts.note: a mark is a figure, as a score in a test

explanation.surface: Worrying about an exploitative figure in capitalism.
explanation.definitionFit: A free market is an economy driven by supply and demand with little state control, the basis of capitalism.

clue.text: Unprofessional activities of Tories duly condemned

indicators.note: condemned letters are broken down and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Political criticism: amateurish conduct by Conservatives gets roundly denounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Home improvement done by amateurs rather than hired tradespeople is unprofessional work.

clue.text: "What a hit!", Ian shrieked, catching number from South Pacific

indicators.note: catching means holding within, so the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: Ian cheers a hit song from the musical South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a song; it is a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahitians are people from Tahiti, a South Pacific island, so a number of islanders.

clue.text: International judge supporting certain type of equality

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits below the others

parts.note: some means certain, as in certain people
to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: An international judge backs a certain kind of equality.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometry is equality of measure, a mapping that preserves distances.

clue.text: Tube of tortoiseshell perhaps not entirely straight

parts.note: a tortoiseshell is a type of cat, hence perhaps

indicators.note: not entirely means one letter short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: hetero means straight, heterosexual

explanation.surface: A tortoiseshell tube that is slightly bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortoiseshell' looks like the material; it is a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A catheter is a thin flexible tube inserted into the body.

clue.text: Pesters a Whig to change statement to the House

indicators.note: to change these letters is to put them in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone nags a Whig politician to alter a statement to the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The House' looks like Parliament, but it is a theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage whisper is an aside spoken loudly enough for the theatre audience, the house, to hear.

clue.text: Outsiders to decolonise Java and Vanuatu, strangely familiar phenomenon

indicators.note: outsiders are the outermost letters of each word

explanation.surface: Decolonising Java and Vanuatu feels like something that has happened before.
explanation.definitionFit: Deja vu is the uncanny feeling of having already experienced the present moment.

clue.text: Federal capital to put up tall wall to exclude students

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means written upward, reversed
to exclude is to keep out, so letters are removed

parts.note: L stands for learner, so students are several of those letters

explanation.surface: A capital city builds a high wall to keep students out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, a federal state.

clue.text: Sound of indifference from pantomime horse

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bored noise coming from a pantomime horse, the two-person costume of British Christmas shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Meh is an interjection expressing boredom or lack of interest.

clue.text: Family member set off, seeming to lack answer

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged
to lack something is to be without it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: apparent means seeming

explanation.surface: A relative sets off, apparently without a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges SET into STEP's first three letters, STE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepparent is a relative by marriage, the spouse of one's parent.

clue.text: Smooth journalists importune crowd

definitions.meaning: to iron flat, as with clothes
to urge or pester someone insistently
a throng, as in the ... of people

explanation.surface: Slick reporters pester a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word covers ironing, the news media, urging insistently and a dense throng.

clue.text: Propose polkaing periodically

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Suggesting a polka dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to intend or propose it.

clue.text: Tickle and excite it a little

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to tease and stimulate something slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to stimulate pleasantly, much as tickling does.

clue.text: Fine boomerangs, in the style of a native Australian

indicators.note: a boomerang comes back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: OK means fine
a la is French for in the style of

explanation.surface: A fine boomerang made the way an Aboriginal Australian would make it.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is a tree-dwelling marsupial found only in Australia.

clue.text: Spouse and smallest offspring picked up pants

indicators.note: picked up as on a microphone, meaning the words are heard

parts.note: a wife is a spouse and runts are the smallest of a litter

explanation.surface: Someone gathers underwear for their spouse and youngest child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like collecting laundry; it means heard. Y-fronts are British men's briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage pants are underpants, and Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs.

clue.text: Source of Vitamin C vital when suffering relapse

indicators.note: a relapse goes backwards, so the words are read from the end

parts.note: something vital is a must
as means when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: Health advice: vitamin C is essential when you suffer a relapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small citrus fruit, rich in vitamin C.
